BiblicalUsage: The achashtaran were the swift mounts of the Persian royal post — mules and camels, and young dromedaries, carrying Mordecai's counter-decree to every province. The posts "went out, being hastened and pressed on by the king's commandment." The word is the hurry of good news racing against a death sentence.
TheologicalSignificance: A mule's name carries no doctrine, and the hurry in the verses is the point — good news racing the king's own couriers to undo a death sentence.
